title: No truth escapes God's intellect; so these determinately true conditionals are objects of his knowledge
source_text: XLIX. Praeterea certum est, & ab omnibus concessum, nullam omnino veritatem qualiscunque sit fugere intellectum divinum: ac proinde cum propositiones de libere futuris, sub conditione saepius exposita, determinatam veritatem habeant, sunt illae quoque divinae scientiae objectum. Adeoque novit Deus quid singulae creaturae possibiles facturae essent, si vellet illas in hoc aut illo statu condere, nec eis quicquam negare eorum quae ad agendum necessaria sunt.
pass_a_gloss: XLIX. Moreover it is certain, and conceded by all, that no truth at all of whatever kind escapes the divine intellect: and therefore since propositions concerning things freely future, under the condition often set forth, have determinate truth, they too are the object of divine knowledge. And so God knows what each possible creature would do, if he willed to found them in this or that state, and to deny them nothing of those things which are necessary for acting.
pass_b_english: Again, it is certain and granted by all that no truth whatever escapes God's intellect. Propositions about free futures, under the condition explained more than once, have determinate truth, so they too are objects of God's knowledge.
God therefore knows what every possible creature would do if he willed to establish it in this or that state and to deny it nothing it needs in order to act.
